result.message: Reviewed the code-review subject a54967db3aba4570bb40b7aa3766400cc886e918bcbc6026b7af39e93581bbca; the supplied .best_kernel.py is byte-for-byte the same source as optimize_definition_output.json best_code and the ledger round-2 solution (sha256 a54967db...), and round 3 (7cb10fae..., geo_mean 0.3962) was correctly reverted, so the reviewed candidate is the intended one. The candidate is a self-contained Triton scatter_add: an out-of-place `run(inp, dim, index, src)` matching the Definition parameter names/order, with (a) a destination-owned last-axis kernel for contiguous full-extent scatters with ncols <= 1700, (b) last-axis atomic kernels over an fp32 staging buffer for fp16/bf16 and directly over out for fp32, and (c) a strided int64 N-d atomic kernel for the general case. I found no P0 code defect: no computation through torch/torch.ops (torch is used only for allocation), no host synchronization, no mutation of inp/index/src, a freshly allocated non-aliasing output, effects.mutates=[] / returns_alias_of={} are honoured, and no test-specific values or shapes are baked into the results (constants such as _DENSE_MAX_COLS=1700, 128/256 block, 8192/1024 blocks are dispatch/tuning heuristics only and do not change computed values). Correctness evidence in the ledger shows 18/18 workloads PASSED on all three rounds with max_abs_error 2.384e-07; the final verification re-measured geo_mean 0.40669 vs the recorded best 0.41522, which is within the drift_factor 2.0 policy with drift=[]. The only findings are advisory P1: an unconditional fp32 accumulation in the destination-owned kernel that would silently lose precision/mis-handle float64 (and integer) inputs that the 9 frozen correctness cases never exercise, a couple of untested input-applicability limits in the generic path, and the fact that the atomic last-dim path used by the 2048x2048 timing shapes is never numerically compared with the reference (timing rows carry abs_err=null). Note: the review_tests stage for this operator was recorded as SKIPPED_EXPLICIT (review.json, subject_sha256 20fb309b...), so tolerances were not independently re-reviewed there; preflight PASSED with num_cases=9 against the same benchmark fingerprint, and evaluate.json (reference_source=primary, geo_mean 0.99967, abs_err 0.0) only shows the catalog definition agrees with the primary reference, not that the optimized candidate does on uncovered paths.
